title: PEEP versus Pplat at a Fixed Tidal Volume
subtitle: Evaluate the effect of positive end-expiratory pressure titration on plateau pressure and driving pressure at a constant tidal volume

patient.summary: Intubated patient with moderate ARDS passively ventilated in volume-control mode with fixed tidal volume.

prediction.question: When PEEP is increased from 5 to 12 cmH2O at a constant tidal volume and respiratory rate, how will plateau pressure (Pplat), peak pressure (Ppeak), and driving pressure change?

whatToLookAtHint: Compare the change in plateau pressure against the change in set PEEP, and calculate the difference between plateau and total PEEP.

reflection.question: When PEEP is raised from 5 to 12 cmH2O at a fixed tidal volume in a patient with constant compliance, why does driving pressure remain unchanged despite the rise in Pplat?

options.text: Driving pressure equals Pplat - total PEEP (VT / C); with constant VT and compliance, the elastic pressure needed to distend the lung is unchanged.
Increasing PEEP automatically reduces airway resistance, keeping driving pressure constant.
Plateau pressure is independent of PEEP on volume-controlled ventilation.
The ventilator automatically lowers tidal volume as PEEP rises to protect against barotrauma.

reflection.explanation: Plateau pressure is the sum of end-expiratory pressure and the elastic pressure required to deliver the tidal volume: Pplat = PEEP + (VT / C). Driving pressure is defined as ΔP = Pplat - PEEP = VT / C. When PEEP is raised from 5 to 12 cmH2O without changing VT or compliance, Pplat rises 1:1 with PEEP (from 20 to 27 cmH2O), but the difference between them (driving pressure) remains 15 cmH2O (constant). Driving pressure only changes if compliance or tidal volume changes.

evidence.claim: Plateau pressure equals PEEP plus driving pressure (VT / Crs); raising PEEP at constant VT and compliance raises Pplat 1:1 while driving pressure remains unchanged.
evidence.source: Bellani G, et al. Driving pressure is a key ventilatory target in ARDS. Intensive Care Med. 2016;42(10):1647-1650.

evidence.claim: The equation of motion dictates that airway pressure is the sum of resistive and elastic recoil pressures.
evidence.source: West JB, Luks AM. West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials. 11th ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
